_readme: Shopware 6 pack knowledge. STABLE: the source-side prefixes/patterns (Shopware namespaces, plugin manifest conventions, decoration and Twig override patterns) change only with a major version. SEED: the two target lists and the portability patterns were derived from general platform knowledge - re-verify Store API route paths and CMS element type names against the project's exact 6.x minor and edition, because Commercial-plan features are not in the open-source repository. `standard_units` stays empty on purpose: it is derived per project from vendor/shopware and the shipped bundles.

entry_point_patterns.store_api: controller extending Shopware\Core\System\SalesChannel\SalesChannelController or an AbstractRoute subclass with _routeScope 'store-api'
entry_point_patterns.admin_api: controller with _routeScope 'api' / 'administration', or an EntityDefinition exposed automatically through /api/<entity>
entry_point_patterns.cms: CmsElementResolver / AbstractCmsElementResolver implementation plus a cms element twig template
entry_point_patterns.queue: Symfony Messenger message handler (#[AsMessageHandler] or messenger.message_handler tag)
entry_point_patterns.app: custom/apps/<App>/manifest.xml with webhooks, admin extensions and app scripts

override_patterns.service_decoration: services.xml <service id="..." decorates="<core id>"> or #[AsDecorator]; the class-name suffix `Decorated` is the community convention
override_patterns.service_replacement: a service definition re-declaring an existing core service id (no decorates attribute) - replaces, does not wrap
override_patterns.tagged_collection_entry: a tagged service replacing or reordering an entry in a core collection (cart processor/collector, rule definition, payment handler, tax provider)
override_patterns.twig_full_override: a template at the same relative path under Resources/views/storefront/** WITHOUT sw_extends - hides the core template completely (high upgrade risk)
override_patterns.twig_block_extension: {% sw_extends '@Storefront/storefront/...' %} plus {% block ... %} - the maintainable variant, classify as extended
override_patterns.entity_extension: class extending Shopware\Core\Framework\DataAbstractionLayer\EntityExtension - adds fields/associations to a core entity
override_patterns.custom_fields: custom field sets (code or admin-created) - data-only extension, admin-created sets exist ONLY in the database
override_patterns.core_patch: a modified file under vendor/shopware, or a plugin class declared inside the Shopware\Core namespace - highest risk, always name the file

deprecation_patterns: full Twig template overrides without sw_extends (break on every core template change)
direct SQL against core tables instead of the DAL (EntityRepository / Criteria)
business logic in Twig templates or in controllers instead of services
PHP plugin code that cannot exist on SaaS (filesystem writes, console commands, raw SQL migrations, custom Messenger workers, custom Rule/FlowAction classes)
session-held state for storefront features instead of cart/context (blocks a headless frontend)
hard-coded prices, tax or shipping logic instead of Rule Builder / price rules
hard-coded notification and mail logic instead of Flow Builder actions
usage of classes marked @internal or @deprecated in shopware/core (check the version's UPGRADE-6.x.md)
integration_signals: Guzzle/HTTP client calls to an ERP, PIM, CRM or tax/shipping provider inside a plugin service
Admin API Sync API payloads (/api/_action/sync) used by an external integration
import_export_profile usage and CSV mapping files
message queue handlers used as an integration buffer
webhooks declared in an app manifest.xml
custom payment handler / tax provider implementations
source_content_component_pattern: cms_page / cms_section / cms_block / cms_slot rows (Shopping Experiences layouts are DATABASE data, not repository files) plus custom CmsElementResolver classes and their Resources/views/storefront/element/cms-element-<name>.html.twig templates; theme content via theme.json and Resources/app/storefront
target_api_endpoint_families: /store-api/category and /store-api/category/{navigationId} (category page incl. its cms page)
/store-api/context and PATCH /store-api/context (sales-channel context: currency, language, shipping/payment, customer)
/store-api/wishlist and /store-api/customer/wishlist/* (wishlist, requires the feature to be enabled)
/store-api/script/{hook} (app scripts as custom Store API endpoints - the SaaS-compatible extension route)
/api/<entity> (Admin API CRUD over every DAL entity, e.g. /api/product, /api/order, /api/customer)
/api/oauth/token (Admin API authentication) and sw-access-key header (Store API authentication)
target_content_component_types: cms element: text
cms element: image
cms element: image-slider
cms element: image-gallery
cms element: youtube-video / vimeo-video
cms element: product-box
cms element: product-slider
cms element: product-listing
cms element: product-name / product-description-reviews / buy-box (product page elements)
cms element: manufacturer-logo
cms element: cross-selling
cms element: category-navigation
cms element: sidebar-filter
cms element: form (contact / newsletter; extended form types in the Commercial plan)
cms element: html (raw markup escape hatch)
cms element: custom app-provided element (app script + admin component)
cms block: image-text, text-on-image, image-bubble-row, gallery-buybox, product-three-column, product-slider, form, sidebar-filter, cross-selling (block presets combining elements)
cms section: default and sidebar section layouts
cms page type: landing page, category listing page, product page, shop page
theme (theme.json with inheritance, config fields, scss/js entry points)
custom fields on core entities (content-bearing only if the frontend reads them)
mail template (with template variables) as transactional content
document template (invoice, delivery note, credit note, cancellation)
SEO URL template (Twig) per sales channel

_stamp.source: seed from general platform knowledge, to be verified
